content:
anya: Quick sync: proposing we require an explicit "namespace" claim on service API keys/JWTs as the canonical tenancy identifier. Cuts ambiguity from aud/header heuristics.

matt: high level +1. main risk is breaking clients that rely on old inference. do we have a soft migration path?

taylor: also: how do we treat platform-level keys that must operate across orgs? wildcard vs special token?

anya: migration plan sketch: 1) library + gateway read/write support for namespace claim, 2) inference fallback with telemetry + deprecation header, 3) tooling for bulk-rotate keys, 4) deny-by-default after N weeks.

sam_sre: telemetry reqs: emit `auth.ns.explicit`, `auth.ns.inferred`, and `auth.ns.missing`. create alert if `auth.ns.inferred` spikes > 5x baseline.

matt: for big customers we'll add a feature-flag to keep permissive mode longer. ops-bot can expose per-customer opt-in.

ops-bot: feature-flag created: `auth.namespace.migration_mode` scope=account level.

julie_pm: product note: docs + customer comms need clear timelines and migration checklist (rotate CLI, SDK update, admin UI).

anya: specifics on token semantics: - if token.claims.namespace exists => authoritative - else if single namespace inferable from aud/header => use but mark inferred - else => deny unless account opt-in

taylor: precedence question: some legacy headers set `X-Project` and `X-Org`. If both present and conflict with inferred, follow explicit claim > header > inference?

anya: yes. precedence: explicit claim > legacy header (if present and consistent) > inference. But we'll deprecate legacy headers too.

matt: RBAC mapping: use namespace to select policy scope. A token with namespace=org:acme should not access project:acme-prod unless role binds that namespace -> project mapping. Document how role resolution works.

anya: agreed. mapping rules: namespace is the primary key; policies can bind at org or project granularity. We'll provide examples in RFC.

sam_sre: logging: redact token contents but persist token fingerprint + namespace resolution path (explicit|header|inferred) for audits. Add sampling for inferred tokens with hashed caller id.

ops-bot: alert: canary rollout scheduled: env=staging pct=10 flag=auth.namespace.migration_mode

julie_pm: timeline suggestion: - week 0: libs + gateway accept namespace - week 2: inference fallback + metrics - week 6: docs + tooling + customer comms - week 12: start gradual deny-by-default (with long-tail opt-outs)

matt: API changes: admin API for key creation should accept `namespace` param. Default to issuer's org if omitted (but log). SDKs should set explicit claim when creating keys.

taylor: edge-case: shared platform integrators that intentionally create keys for multiple customers. For them provide `namespace=platform` and require an allowlist + stronger auditing. No wildcards.

anya: good call. disallow `*` wildcard. reserve `platform` and `global` values for internal use only and require approval.

sam_sre: ops playbook: how to roll back if false positives spike? -> immediately flip migration_mode per-account to permissive and fallback inference on. Also route exec team to revoke offending keys.

anya: I'll draft RFC follow-up with code snippets, migration CLI, and monitoring runbook. expect PR by tomorrow EOD.

matt: please include sample envoy/middleware config and a policy example for test envs.

anya: sample policy for testing:
```
# deny if namespace missing unless account is opted-in
allow if token.namespace != null and token.namespace == resource.namespace
denied_default = token.namespace == null and not account.opted_in_migration
```

julie_pm: thanks, this is great. I'll prep customer comms draft once RFC lands.

anya: thanks all. continuing in RFC: /r/rfcs/2026-03-authn-namespace-playbook
